subject: DPA amendment request — operational proof of no-model-learning & prompt/response custody for APAC pilot
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@novaterra.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: DPA amendment request — operational proof of no-model-learning & prompt/response custody for APAC pilot

Hi Evelyn / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving this into a pilot (APAC clinical channel) and legal + security have asked for the following updates to the DPA before we can onboard production traffic:

1) Explicit "no model learning / no adaptive training" clause — not just a policy statement in the SOW. We need a contract line that forbids Redwood from using Novaterra data to improve model weights or to create derivative models.
2) Prompt/response custody language — Novaterra retains ownership of inputs and outputs, and Redwood must not assert derivative rights or export derivatives.
3) Subprocessor restrictions — please provide an explicit allowed-subprocessor list for the APAC pilot and an operational path for any future additions (30-day notice + attestation).
4) Operational proof — examples of artifacts we can accept as evidence (KMS key residency proof, audit log slices, KV cache purge logs, SFTP export proof).

I’ve attached a redline (Novaterra_Redline_DPA_v3.docx) with suggested contract text in Sections 3, 7 and the subprocessor addendum. Can you confirm Redwood can provide the operational artifacts above and whether the platform can scope a tenant-only configuration for us (APAC region, dedicated pool / dedicated routing)?

We’d like a negotiated redline and signature in ~2 weeks if possible (target go/no-go: 2025-04-29). Let me know if you want to take an internal ops call first.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lim
Head of Legal Ops, Novaterra Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@novaterra.health>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA amendment request — operational proof of no-model-learning & prompt/response custody for APAC pilot

Sara — thanks for the clear list and the redline. We can support the commercial ask; below is a summary of options and the artifacts we can produce. Happy to jump on a 30–45 minute ops/legal sync today or tomorrow to align.

Summary of what Redwood can commit now:
- Contract language: we can add an explicit "no adaptive training / no model updates" clause and a definition for "derivative" and "derivative models" in the DPA.
- Prompt/response custody: we’ll accept language that customers retain ownership of inputs/outputs and will add a cross-reference to the exportability section.
- Subprocessors: we can provide an APAC-specific allowed-subprocessor snapshot (current list) and an addendum workflow: 30-day notice + customer opt-out window + third-party attestation on request.
- Operational artifacts (examples we can deliver): KMS key metadata (key IDs + region and exposure matrix), tenant-level audit log slices, KV/cache purge job logs (timestamped), SFTP export confirmation records, and signed attestations from our infra team describing routing and segregation.

Technical path options for pilot (we'll follow whichever procurement/legal prefer):
A) Dedicated tenant + dedicated GPU pool (isolated compute, private routing) + customer-managed KMS (preferred for highest assurance).
B) Shared tenant + strict subprocessor whitelist + encrypted ephemeral KV with scheduled purge + additional logging and attestation.

Next steps I propose: 1) we review your attached redline and deliver a Redwood redline by EOD tomorrow; 2) ops (David) will produce a short "artifact pack" template so you can confirm acceptance criteria; 3) sign-off target 2025-04-29.

If that works, I’ll schedule the internal call and copy the Novaterra legal contact you prefer.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@novaterra.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Keegan <tom.keegan@novaterra.health>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA amendment request — operational proof of no-model-learning & prompt/response custody for APAC pilot

Evelyn — that plan sounds good. A couple clarifications from legal/security:
- We need the contract language to say "no model updates" (explicit) and also to bar creation, distribution, or licensing of any derivative models that are trained on Novaterra data.
- For subprocessors, we require an attestation if any new subprocessor processes Novaterra data; attestation must include specific controls, location, and whether HSM/KMS is used.
- Operational artifacts: the KMS metadata must show residency in APAC (ap-southeast-1) for the keys used for Novaterra tenant; audit log slices should include at-minimum: request IDs, timestamps, and the route taken (region/model variant).

DocuSign is preferred for execution. 2-week timeline still looks OK on our side. If you can send the Redwood redline and the ops artifact template today, we’ll review and escalate internally.

Sara

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@novaterra.health>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Apr 2025 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA amendment request — operational proof of no-model-learning & prompt/response custody for APAC pilot

Sara / Evelyn — quick ops note with what we can produce and a pragmatic implementation sketch. Attaching an ops PDF with example artifacts (ops_implementation_notes.pdf).

Implementation sketch (pilot):
- Deployment: Dedicated GPU pool in ap-southeast-1; single-tenant routing to isolate Novaterra traffic.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys supported. We can either provide customer HSM integration (bring-your-own-key) or create a tenant key seeded only for Novaterra with strict IAM binding. Metadata we can export: key ID, region, creation timestamps, key rotation history.
- Subprocessors: current APAC subprocessors = 3rd-party CDN (edge cache), storage provider (SFTP partner), monitoring vendor. We will produce a frozen snapshot list for the addendum. Any future addition follows 30-day notice + attestation flow.
- Audit evidence: we can provide a signed audit slice containing request IDs, node IDs, model variant IDs, timestamps, and KV purge job logs (showing purge completion and checksum).
- Performance: Dedicated pool will increase costs; expect ~15–20% throughput variance during early ramp as we pin capacity.

Acceptable evidence bundle (examples):
1) KMS export (metadata only, not private keys) — JSON summary with key IDs and regions.
2) Audit log slice — gzipped CSV (time-limited access link).
3) KV purge job log — timestamped run showing deleted cache keys.
4) Signed attestation PDF from Redwood infra lead.

If Novaterra requires HSM-managed keys on your side, we’ll need the handshake details to validate integration. Happy to join a technical call to walk through log formats and the attestation template.

-David
David Kim
Director, Platform Ops — Redwood Inference
[attachment: ops_implementation_notes.pdf]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@novaterra.health>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Apr 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA amendment request — operational proof of no-model-learning & prompt/response custody for APAC pilot

Sara — thanks for the quick confirmations. Per David’s note and our redline review (see attached: Novaterra_Redline_DPA_v3.docx — Redwood_response_redline.docx attached in DocuSign), next steps:

1) Redwood will deliver: a Redwood redline (done), an ops artifact template (attached), and a frozen allowed-subprocessor snapshot for APAC.
2) Novaterra confirms acceptance criteria for each artifact type (i.e., which fields in the audit slice unlock acceptance).
3) We’ll run a short validation run (non-prod traffic) and provide the artifact bundle after completion.

Required artifacts list to be delivered after pilot validation: KMS metadata export, tenant-scoped audit slice, KV purge logs, signed attestation. If Novaterra prefers a BYOK/HSM model we’ll coordinate key exchange and validate via a short handshake.

I’ll schedule a 45-minute joint call (technical + legal) for Monday 2025-04-21 to finalize the addendum language and DocuSign flow. Please confirm availability.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
